text:
maria-support: escalation from AcmePayments — multiple customers reporting intermittent 5xx and long tail timeouts on hosted inference (p95->p999 spike). getting lots of customer-facing 504s and some 502s. example request id: rq_acme_20260317_89ab.

kevin-eng: ack. can you paste a representative request and any correlation ids? rough symptom is queue saturation + long continuous-batching backlog?

maria-support: here's a sanitized curl from customer (they're sending batch of short prompts at high rate):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-xxxx' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"model":"open-3b","inputs":["Summarize this...","Summarize that..."]}'
```
we're seeing gateway logs: `gateway: enqueue_ms=2450 queue_depth=896 continuous_batch_backlog=72 enqueue_rejects=4` and the upstream returns `504 deadline exceeded`. also some `upstream closed connection` 502s.

sarah-sre: that queue_depth number is the clue. tenant burst likely pushed the ingress queue past soft limit and continuous batcher couldn't drain — KV cache miss churn also visible. any billing/auth spikes? sometimes runaway retries from token refreshes cause loops.

maria-support: customer confirmed they rolled out a background job last night that fan-outs many short requests. not an auth error AFAICT.

opsbot: incident created: ITP-6123. runbook link: https://internal.runbooks/queue-surge (runbook: temp-throttle, route-to-dedicated, disable-continuous-batching). Paging on-call eng. :rotating_light:

kevin-eng: quick mitigation options: 1) throttle tenant at gateway (reject early, 429) 2) enable tenant bypass to dedicated pool (if reserved capacity exists) 3) flip continuous_batching=false for that tenant so we avoid backlog merging. I'll try 1 and 3 first.

james-plat: prepared a bypass route: `route add tenant=acme-payments -> pool=dedicated-us-east:acme-dedicated-01` (will take ~30s to propagate).

kevin-eng: also pushing a temporary config to the ingress: `max_queue_depth=256` and `early_reject_threshold=200` for tenant acme-payments. command: `infractl ingress update --tenant acme-payments --max-queue-depth 256 --early-reject 200`

sarah-sre: good. also increase KV cache warming TTL for that tenant to reduce cold hits: `kvcache.set_ttl tenant=acme 300s` — that will help continuous batcher drain faster.

maria-support: applied throttles, started routing a fraction to dedicated pool. customer reports immediate drop in 504s on dedicated route, but hosted pool still showing tail 5xxs.

kevin-eng: I'm going to disable continuous batching for tenant on hosted cluster while ingress drains backlog: `config update tenant=acme continuous_batching=false` — patched.

support-bot: config change accepted. telemetry shows continuous_batching=false for acme-payments in host cluster-1.

opsbot: pager update: mitigation in progress. autoclose window 60m.

maria-support: update from customer: errors down by ~70% after routing partial traffic, but p99 tail is still elevated for remaining hosted traffic. they want a root-cause and long-term fix.

kevin-eng: root-cause hypothesis: sudden burst caused large queue_depth + sustained continuous-batching backlog. continuous batching groups short requests which increases per-batch token work; when backlog grows, KV cache misses amplify work and drain time increases -> tail latency spiral. We need either stronger early-rejects, per-tenant rate limits, or model sharding to smaller batches.

james-plat: engineering suggestion for long-term: 1) per-tenant burst bucket with hard cap + token-bucket smoothing 2) dynamic continuous-batching disable when queue_depth>threshold 3) autoscale warm pools faster when many short requests detected. Also recommend adding a dedicated fast-path for small short-prompt workloads (no kv cache heavy ops).

elaine-csm: flagged to Acme CSM. they were surprised because hosted SLA said best-effort but they expected smoother degradation. offering to move them to Dedicated as part of support plan.

maria-support: customer asked if billing could have caused a sudden reject — they saw no billing alerts. but we should watch for auth retry storms (refresh tokens) as a root cause in other incidents.

kevin-eng: logs snapshot for one host process capturing the tail behavior:
```
[2026-03-17T21:12:08Z] req=rq_acme_20260317_89ab enqueue_ms=2453 queue_depth=912 cb_backlog=78 kv_miss=12 backend_ms=12000 upstream_err=504
[2026-03-17T21:12:09Z] req=rq_acme_20260317_89ac enqueue_ms=2601 queue_depth=918 cb_backlog=82 backend_ms=13000 upstream_err=504
[2026-03-17T21:12:10Z] req=rq_acme_20260317_89ad enqueue_ms=780 queue_depth=920 cb_backlog=88 backend_ms=10 upstream_ok
```

kevin-eng: note last line — some requests slip through quickly (cache hits) while others get massive backend_ms because they hit cold paths. that's consistent with KV churn + batching grouping causing variance.

sarah-sre: action items for incident writeup: - confirm severity and impacted customers - timeline of config changes - telemetry dumps (queue depth, cb_backlog, kv_miss rate) - customer repro artifacts - runbook steps executed. I'll take ownership of the timeline.

maria-support: customer pleased with partial mitigation, asked for ETA for full fix. recommended temporary Dedicated migration + platform follow-ups.

james-plat: followups: implement dynamic continuous-batching gating (disable when queue_depth>X), add per-tenant early-reject telemetry, and add a small-prompt fast-path. I'll open tickets and link to this thread. ticket: ENG-1429 (dynamic cb gating), ENG-1430 (small-prompt fast-path).

opsbot: incident update posted to status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/ITP-6123.

maria-support: thanks team. closing pager for now; will keep thread open for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
